lib.title: Pocket PC Software Library
lib.intro: We have actually imported and run the Pocket PC software that circulated back then. Titles marked “Ready to play” download and start with one click; the rest are listed for reference, explaining whether they can be emulated and what makes them hard, with search keywords to help you find your own legal copy.
lib.none: No matching software. Try a different keyword or filter.
h.020: Beginner's guide: start playing in three steps
h.021: First time here? Follow these steps and you'll be playing your first game within five minutes.
h.023: Pick a title marked “Ready to play” in the “Pocket PC Software Library” below and click “Download and play”. Your own game packages are usually a .zip, .cab or .exe installer; no need to extract them or pick a processor version.
h.025: Click “Import game” above and choose the file you just downloaded. The emulator unpacks the installer, finds the game and picks the right version automatically; it then appears in “My Library”.
h.026: Downloaded programs are never executed, only unpacked and inspected. If a file can't be understood, you'll be told why and what to do next.
h.028: Click a game's name to start; press ‹ Library to come back
h.030: <kbd>↑</kbd><kbd>↓</kbd><kbd>←</kbd><kbd>→</kbd> to move, <kbd>Enter</kbd> for the action button, <kbd>Esc</kbd> to go back
h.031: Below the screen: a D-pad disc, soft keys and the A / B / C buttons, for mouse or finger
h.032: Progress saves automatically; the “⋯” menu lets you download, import or reset saves
h.033: Screen lying on its side? Click “Rotate screen” above; landscape games back then were played with the device turned sideways
h.035: If you run into any of these situations, just follow the steps.
h.038: Left mouse button / tap the screen
h.047: The game says MFC is missing
h.048: Some programs need mfcce300.dll, which is built into Pocket PC. A “Get MFC automatically and restart” button appears above the game screen; just click it. This site downloads the Pocket PC 2000 SDK that Microsoft offered for free back then from archive.org, and adds only the files the game needs.
h.049: To do it by hand: open the SDK with 7-Zip, extract Program Files/mfc/lib/arm/mfcce300.dll and olece300.dll (for MIPS or SH3 games, use the mips or sh3 folder instead), then import them together with the game.
h.051: When you click “Import game” you can select several files at the same time, for example a game's .cab plus mfcce300.dll, or the game itself plus its data files. This site combines them into one game package for you, so there's no need to zip them yourself.
h.053: Progress is saved in your browser every 10 seconds. In the library, click “⋯ › Download save” next to a game to get a .zip; on another computer, the Windows app or the Android app, use “⋯ › Import save” to pick up where you left off.
h.054: Play on a phone or tablet
h.055: Just open this site in your phone's browser to play. A D-pad and A / B / C buttons appear at the bottom of the screen; in landscape, the buttons move to the sides. To play offline, install the Android app.
h.056: What if a game won't open
h.057: The screen explains the reason and next step in plain language, such as “This is a desktop program” or “This is a .NET program”. Most downloads include several processor versions, and this site picks one automatically. You can also check the compatibility list for this software's test results.
h.059: Instead of emulating an entire device, it reimplements Windows CE in Rust, so it starts fast and needs no ROM.
h.060: Three processorsVersions for ARM (iPAQ, Axim), MIPS (Casio Cassiopeia) and SH3 (HP Jornada) all run.
h.061: Understands downloadsInstallers, self-extracting archives, nested CABs and even 1999-era archive formats are unpacked to find the game automatically.
h.062: Saves work everywhereThe same save zip moves freely between the web, Windows and Android versions.
h.063: Tested on over a thousand titlesAll 1,443 downloads on archive.org have been tested, and the compatibility list records the result for each one.
h.066: Do I need a Pocket PC ROM or system files?
h.067: No. Most games run as is. Programs that use MFC need mfcce300.dll: a “Get MFC automatically” button appears on the game screen, and this site extracts it from Microsoft's Pocket PC 2000 SDK on archive.org. You can also open the SDK with 7-Zip yourself, extract Program Files/mfc/lib/arm/mfcce300.dll, and import it together with the game.
h.068: Where are my games and saves stored? Are they uploaded?
h.069: Everything stays in this browser (IndexedDB) and is never uploaded to any server. Clearing site data deletes it too, so back up first with “⋯ › Download save”.
h.071: The emulator doesn't implement every Windows CE feature yet. .NET programs, x86 versions and some installers aren't supported for now. The compatibility list shows every tested title and the reason.
h.072: Can I play offline on a computer or phone?
h.073: Yes, download the Windows and Android apps. They have the same features and save format as the web version.
h.074: Can I open it in two tabs at once?
h.075: No. Two tabs would overwrite each other's progress, so the second tab stops at a notice screen.
h.076: PocketPC3630 is open source under the MIT or Apache 2.0 license, forked from PocketHLE. It includes no games or Microsoft files; please use only software you have obtained legally. GitHub · Compatibility list · Download for Windows / Android
h.078: Game screen on its side? Turn it around
h.081: This game needs the MFC system files built into Pocket PC.
h.085: Just import the files you downloaded. For files it doesn't recognize, the emulator uses its knowledge base to dig out the game inside, and it never runs downloaded programs.
h.088: A .zip with one .cab at the top level, optionally with extra files (such as mfcce300.dll)
h.089: A .zip of the game's installed folder, such as quake/PocketQuake.exe
h.091: Desktop installers (setup.exe) or downloads with one CAB per processor: the ARM version is picked automatically
h.093: Games that use MFC need mfcce300.dll, which is built into Pocket PC (some also need olece300.dll); the emulator doesn't include it. Put a copy from your own device into the .zip, at the same level as the .cab. If it's missing, you'll be told before the game starts.
h.096: SH4 programs that use floating-point instructions, and x86 versions
h.099: A save .zip contains the game's saves/ folder and pockethle-registry.dat, and works across the Windows, Android and web versions.

lib.reason.blank: Starts, but the screen stays blank
lib.reason.early: Exits on its own shortly after starting
lib.reason.noframes: Starts, but hasn't drawn anything yet
lib.reason.system: Needs system files built into the device (such as MFC); the web version can usually add them automatically
lib.reason.api: Uses Windows CE features the emulator doesn't implement yet
lib.reason.files: Required data files aren't in the download
lib.reason.dotnet: .NET Compact Framework program; needs a full .NET runtime
lib.reason.exe: The program file can't be loaded
lib.reason.instr: Uses processor instructions the emulator doesn't support yet
lib.reason.noppc: No Pocket PC program file was found in the download; it may be wrapped in another installer format
lib.reason.desktop: The download is a PC installer; the Pocket PC version could not be extracted from it
lib.reason.badcab: The installer isn't in Pocket PC format or is corrupted
lib.reason.notprogram: This is a development tool, firmware or documentation, not a program that runs on the device
lib.reason.uirect: The program reports “Bad UI rectangle”; the input panel window position it needs isn't provided yet
lib.reason.bmp: The program reports that loading an image resource failed
lib.reason.tree: The program uses tree view features that aren't supported yet
lib.reason.driver: The program needs the device's hardware driver information
lib.reason.expired: The trial period has expired; this isn't an emulator problem
